correctness.rationale: The matrix action and all commutator powers are explicitly computed. For nonzero cyclic exponents, T^j-I=N u_j(N) with invertible u_j(N), proving constant kernel/image. This supports exact conjugacy orbits, irreducible character degrees by cyclic Clifford induction, every conditional commutator fiber, and the convolution law. Jordan partitions have common n=2p,b=p, but nilpotency indices p-1 and 2; N^(p-1)=0 also proves exponent p. Exhaustive small-order class-orbit enumeration for p=5,7 and rank checks in the large families agree. The infinite theorem uses proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The specific joint counterexample requires all of equal order, exponent p, full class-size multiplicity vectors, full complex-character-degree multiplicity vectors, all orientable surface-word output distributions, and different (unboundedly separated) nilpotency classes. Fernández-Alcober–Moretó addresses possible counts of distinct values in class-two groups; Mann records unbounded class with three class sizes but not matched vectors. O’Brien–Voll provides a broad enumeration mechanism, which can specialize to the class/character part, but no inspected assertion gives the simultaneous paired collision and surface-word part. Ito–Mann is a residual plausible antecedent, not decisively compared in full text. Earlier related cyclic-by-cyclic surface-word twins do not establish the extra exponent or simultaneous full class/character multiplicities. The combined claim has not been established as previously covered in the searched sources; priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: Original full text of Ito and Mann (2006), Counting classes and characters of groups of prime exponent, was not accessible through the available arXiv/open-access searches; its abstract concerns relatively free groups and no decisive direct implication was identified. A broader fixed-rank unipotent-module theorem could potentially subsume the class/character part.

Existing Lie orbit formulas of O’Brien and Voll apply to class and character vectors generally; this result only claims the particular combined indistinguishability with surface-word distributions and exponent p, not novelty of generic enumerators.
Publication priority is not externally certified; unpublished work or more general group-theoretic equivalences may exist.

value.rationale: This is a motivated unbounded-family counterexample to the joint distinguishing power of several natural invariants of finite p-groups, stronger than separately showing two small sets or one word law cannot detect nilpotency class. It supplies exact multiplicities and all output fibers, and isolates the structural reason (nilpotency index is invisible once n and ker dimension are fixed) without claiming a broad classification or new Clifford theory.
